text:
ops-bot: [ALERT] Nightdash perf: runtime-serving-prod 99p latency +45% (23:10-23:30 UTC). throughput -18%. KV cache hit rate dropped 98% -> 84%. avg batch size 6.2 -> 3.1. Suspect kernel selection/heuristics change. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dash/abc123

maya: saw it, 👀. Any deploys around 23:00?

ci-bot: Deploy log: rollout deploy-2026-03-17-22:55 (PR #4512) to runtime/serving cluster. Canary started 22:57 UTC.

derek: PR #4512 is the kernel-selection heuristics rewrite (changed prefer_fast_threshold and fallback policy).

naveen: i'll kick off a bisect on runtime repo against canary commit range now.

maya: also nightly CI perf job flagged a regression: perf-nightly-runtime failed with +18% 99p. Link: https://ci.redwood/jobs/perf-nightly/9876

ci-bot: Perf job log: increased tail during KV eviction window, batch sizes dropped across requests. Relevant section: `kv::lookup` latency spike at 23:12.

derek: can someone grab a quick CPU profile on canary? try a flamegraph for the 23:10-23:30 window.

naveen: running `perf record -F 99 -g -- ./serve --workload=nightly-test --duration=900s` now.

naveen: pprof summary (sampling):
```
runtime::kernel_selector::select_kernel 48%
batching::choose_strategy 22%
kv::lookup 12%
copy::memcpy 8%
other 10%
```

liz: select_kernel at 48% matches my hypothesis. PR #4512 added a fallback path that probes a different kernel and does extra KV validation for quantized variants. That probe looks expensive under eviction.

maya: can we pause the rollout?

ops-bot: Deploy bot: Rollout deploy-2026-03-17 paused automatically due to performance alert (policy: perf-slo-guard).

sam: temp mitigation idea: force the old threshold in runtime config to avoid triggering fallback. e.g. set `runtime.kernel_selection.prefer_fast_threshold=0.9` (previous was 0.9, new default is 0.7). I can flip it on canary.

derek: create a revert PR too, if bisect points to that commit. We should be ready to rollback quickly.

naveen: git bisect results: culprit commit `abc1234` (PR #4512). Confirmed by running perf test before/after.

naveen: bisect commands used:
```
git bisect start HEAD abc0000
git bisect bad HEAD
git bisect good abc0000
# ran perf harness and checked 99p
```

derek: thanks. opened PR #4520 to revert commit abc1234 and pinned config change as emergency fallback. https://git.redwood/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4520

maya: plan for next steps:
1) revert in canary (PR #4520) and validate perf night run
2) if canary good, roll revert to prod with 10% stepups
3) follow-up: update heuristics and add perf unit test to catch this pattern
4) add regression alert on KV hit-rate delta + batch size drop

liz: i'll own the follow-up (adjust heuristics & perf test). I'll also add a small perf sim harness for eviction-heavy workloads.

sam: canary config patch applied: set prefer_fast_threshold=0.9 on canary workers. Restarted 6 pods -> monitoring.

maya: great. @naveen can you re-run the pprof after revert applied?

naveen: on it. re-running now, will post summary in ~5m.

naveen: post-revert quick profile: select_kernel down to 18%, batching choose_strategy down to 9%, KV lookup stable. 99p back within 3% of baseline.

derek: excellent. will coordinate the production rollback window.

maya: add a note to the release notes and mention we paused PR #4512 until heuristics updated.

liz: filing follow-up issue: https://jira.redwood/browse/RW-9872 — will include perf test and an automated smoke that simulates eviction.

derek: thumbs up. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

maya: summary: detected nightly perf regression -> traced to kernel selector changes in PR #4512 -> bisected to commit abc1234 -> applied config mitigation and reverted in canary -> perf restored -> follow-up for test and heuristic fix assigned to liz.

ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0317-01 (perf regression, rollback).

maya: closing the thread, will update on prod rollback schedule.

derek: ok, monitoring dashboards for next 2 hours.

sam: oncall will watch alerts.

liz: will post PR for heuristic fix by EOD tomorrow.

maya: thanks everyone.
